I am pretty sure that I want to live abroad when I grow up. Of course, I enjoy living in my own country, South Korea. I'm comfortable with the culture here.
I think most Koreans are respectful and hardworking people. My foreign friends all seem to like it very much. They say the people are friendly, and they really like the food.
Still, one thing I heard my foreign friends say about my country is that there isn't much diversity.
For example, although it's true that people in Jeolla-do and Gangwon-do speak with different accents and eat slightly different foods, it feels like everyone in Korea is pretty similar.

Therefore, I know that if I want to meet many different kinds of people in my life, I will have to travel abroad. I already have foreign friends, so I know that people in other countries are different.
Besides speaking different languages, I think it's fascinating how people are different. There are so many differences between cultures. It's hard to think of just one to talk about.

Still, I can say that I enjoy the stories that foreigners tell me. Also, by talking to them, I can inform them about life in Korea and help them understand my own culture. In my opinion, this makes everyone better off.
If I travel abroad, I know I'll be able to see some cool sights, but the best part will be meeting people and hearing stories.
I live in the USA. Because of its immense size and diverse heritage, my country has one of the most complex cultural identities in the world. Our country has many very different places and people.
For example, in the northeastern U.S., there are forests and many large cities. In different areas, there are plains, tall mountains, and deserts.
Northern areas get lots of snow, while in places like Florida and Southern California, it is warm all year and there are even palm trees.
I love traveling around the country with my family. Everywhere I go, there are new things to see.
The other remarkable thing about America is the many different kinds of Americans you'll meet. Depending on geography, people in different places lead all sorts of different lifestyles.
America is a nation of immigrants who came from all over the world. Different groups have different traditions and cultures.
I think I could spend the rest of my life learning about American culture. That's why, when I travel, I want to keep going places in my own country.

In 2001, Dennis Tito became the world's first space tourist. Mr. Tito is an American engineer and businessman. He is a very wealthy millionaire with a large fortune.
After a long career as an engineer designing airplanes, Mr. Tito wanted to fulfill his dream of flying in space, even though he wasn't an astronaut.
Determined to visit space, Mr. Tito paid the Russian government $20 million of his own money to fly into space on a Russian rocket. He flew into space on April 28, 2001.

In space, Mr. Tito visited the International Space Station and orbited the earth for almost 8 days. He also did some science experiments that he said were helpful to his engineering company. He came back to earth on May 6.
Before Mr. Tito's flight, only professional astronauts chosen by countries had ever flown in space. His flight created a new industry: space tourism.
By 2009, six more wealthy space tourists had paid Russia $20–35 million each to fly in space. Today, private companies also send tourists into space.
Space tourism is still very new, and flying in space is still very expensive.
However, more and more companies want to make money from it. For many people, this is an exciting idea.
However, not everyone is happy about space tourism. Before Mr. Tito's flight, many astronauts and scientists at NASA refused to help with his training.
They thought space travel should be for scientific research, not for profit.

The Apollo program was NASA's third human spaceflight program. It landed the first humans on the Moon from 1969 to 1972.
Apollo ran from 1961 to 1972, with the first crewed flight in 1968.
The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990, and it is still working today.
It was not the first space telescope, but it is one of the largest. It is an important research tool for astronomers.
The Voyager program uses two robotic space probes, Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, to study the outer Solar System.
The probes were launched in 1977, when Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune were lined up in a good way for the trip.
The International Space Station is a space station in low Earth orbit. It was first launched in 1998.
It is a joint project of five space agencies: NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA, and CSA. Who owns and uses the station is decided by intergovernmental treaties and agreements.
